1	# Servers and Drivers
2	
3	Conventions for the user-space half of minix.rs: how a server or driver crate is built and branded,
4	how it reaches its receive loop, how it finds its peers, how PM drives the process lifecycle, and
5	the request/reply contracts that bind every band. The kernel-side halves of these rules live in
6	[kernel.md](./kernel.md); request numbers, band bases, payload offsets and the ABI freeze live in
7	[abi.md](./abi.md); the lint and arithmetic traps that bite server code live in
8	[rust-style.md](./rust-style.md). Link across, never duplicate.
9	
10	## Building a user-space server
11	
12	User-space servers build as freestanding `#![no_std]`/`#![no_main]` ELFs linked with their own
13	`user.ld` (page-aligned PT_LOADs, base `0x10_0000`; the kernel sets `sp_el0`, so `_start` needs no
14	stack setup). Since M1 the kernel's `build.rs` builds them for the **custom target
15	`tools/targets/aarch64-unknown-minixrs.json`** (the pinned nightly's `aarch64-unknown-none` spec
16	plus `"os": "minixrs"`; regenerate on nightly bumps with `rustc -Zunstable-options --print
17	target-spec-json --target aarch64-unknown-none` and re-apply the `"os"` line) via
18	`-Zjson-target-spec -Zbuild-std=core,alloc -Zbuild-std-features=compiler-builtins-mem`, all into
19	**one shared** nested `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (`target/minixrs-user` — separate from the outer `target/`
20	root, so nested cargo can't deadlock on the kernel build's lock, but shared across the 9 crates so
21	build-std compiles core/alloc once, not 9×).
22	
23	The `-T<user.ld>` link arg comes from **each crate's own `build.rs`**, cfg-gated on `target_os =
24	"minixrs"` (host `check`/`clippy` stay linker-flag-free); `kernel/build.rs` injects no rustflags and
25	scrubs inherited ones. `boot_image/elf.rs` is the minimal ET_EXEC/AArch64 loader (PT_LOAD →
26	`alloc_frame` + HHDM copy + map; BSS via zeroed frames). The workspace `[workspace.lints.rust]
27	unexpected_cfgs` check-cfg shim in the root `Cargo.toml` is what keeps host clippy green on the
28	`"minixrs"` cfg — delete it at M5 when the real rustc target exists.
29	
30	`-Zjson-target-spec` must be passed **explicitly** at that call site even if your builds work
31	without it: a *global* `~/.cargo/config.toml` carrying `[unstable] json-target-spec = true`
32	(RustRover needs one for `.json` specs) silently satisfies the gate on your machine while CI, which
33	has no such file, fails the nested build. Same class of trap for any unstable cargo flag — reproduce
34	a suspected config-masking failure with `CARGO_UNSTABLE_<FLAG>=false cargo …`, which overrides the
35	config the way a bare CI runner does.
36	
37	### Branding
38	
39	Every user-space binary crate invokes `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()` at the crate root, emitting the
40	28-byte minixrs ELF identity note (owner `"minixrs\0"`, type 1, `[abi_version=1, flags=0]`; spec in
41	the tooling repo's `docs/abi-note.md`) into `.note.minixrs.ident` — a dedicated PT_NOTE phdr at the
42	start of the RO PT_LOAD, per the `user.ld` dual-assignment rule (`KEEP()` is mandatory, and the rule
43	must stay ahead of the `/DISCARD/ *(.note.*)` line).
44	
45	The kernel **refuses unbranded ELFs**: `kernel-shared::brand::scan_brand` (pure, host-tested) runs
46	in `elf::load_into` (`ElfError::MissingBrand`/`UnsupportedAbi` → `[brand] reject: …` trace, then
47	boot panic / exec `ENOMEM`) and again as a pack-time assertion in `kernel/build.rs` — so a new
48	binary crate that forgets `brand!()` fails the kernel build, not the boot. `[brand]` traces appear
49	only on failure; a healthy boot has none.
50	
51	### Watching dependencies
52	
53	When a boot server gains a new path dependency, add that crate's `src` dir to `kernel/build.rs`'s
54	server `rerun-if-changed` list (a directory is watched recursively) — otherwise edits to the dep
55	silently embed a stale server ELF. That list covers *shared* inputs only (`minixrs-ipc`,
56	`server-rt`, `kernel-shared`, `minixrs-abi-note`, plus the target JSON); a newly added boot crate
57	needs no entry of its own — `build_server` already watches each crate's
58	`src`/`user.ld`/`Cargo.toml`/`build.rs`.
59	
60	### ELF-only attributes, and why `forbid(unsafe_code)` is unusable
61	
62	ELF-only attributes on server crates (`#[unsafe(link_section = ".text._start")]`, etc.) must be
63	`#[cfg_attr(target_os = "minixrs", ...)]`-gated (the M1 target; they read `"none"` before that) —
64	`cargo check --workspace` also builds servers for the Mach-O host, which rejects ELF section
65	specifiers.
66	
67	Relatedly, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` is unusable on any freestanding binary crate here — edition
68	2024's `unsafe(no_mangle)` / `unsafe(link_section)` on `_start` trip the `unsafe_code` lint — so a
69	crate with no `unsafe` *block* (e.g. `drivers/memory`) says so in its crate docs instead of
70	asserting it with the attribute.
71	
72	## Verifying server behaviour
73	
74	User-space servers run at EL0 with no console access — they cannot print. Verify server behaviour
75	through kernel-side traces (`[pf]` from `do_page_fault`, `[ksys …]` from `do_vmctl`/`system`, `[ipc
76	N]` from `ipc::dispatch`), never server-side logging.
77	
78	Trace sampling is asymmetric: `[ipc N]` head-traces the first ~12 calls *plus* every 100th, but
79	`[ksys N]` samples only every 100th (no head carve-out) — a server's first or rare kernel call (e.g.
80	a startup `SYS_GETINFO`) shows on `[ipc]`, not `[ksys]`.
81	
82	Since slice 5.1 a server can also use `SYS_DIAGCTL` through `server-rt::diag_print`; see
83	[kernel.md](./kernel.md) for the debug channel's kernel half.
84	
85	## SEF: the receive loop
86	
87	System servers drive their receive loop through `server-rt`'s SEF (slice 4.1+):
88	
89	```rust
90	let sef = sef_startup(SefConfig { init_fresh, signal_handler });
91	loop {
92	    if sef.receive(&mut msg) != OK { continue }
93	    match msg.m_type { /* … */ }
94	}
95	```
96	
97	Callbacks pass via the config struct and are carried in the returned `Sef` handle (no global
98	`setcb`/static state, so `server-rt` is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). `sef_startup` learns the
99	server's endpoint and name via `SYS_GETINFO(GET_WHOAMI)` (through `server-rt::sys_getinfo`),
100	announces the server via `diag_print`, and `sef.receive` filters SEF control messages, returning
101	only application messages.
102	
103	The pure classifier lives in `server-rt/src/classify.rs` (host-tested; the IPC glue in `sef.rs` is
104	coverage-excluded like the server `main.rs`es) and gates each control event on `m_source`, not
105	`m_type` alone — NOTIFY ping from RS, `SEF_SIGNAL` from PM/RS, `SEF_INIT` from RS — so a client
106	holding only an `ipc_to` bit to the server can't spoof a signal or init.
107	
108	Shared client-side helpers belong in `server-rt`, not in per-server copies: `payload.rs`
109	(`rd_i32`/`wr_i32`/`rd_u64`/`wr_u64`/`buf_addr`), `kcall.rs` (`sys_safecopy`/`sys_copy`),
110	`diag_fmt`, `sys_getinfo`, `sef_retrieve_from_ds`, and `cdev.rs`'s four-field CDEV parse. Payload
111	accessors use `checked_add` — see [rust-style.md](./rust-style.md).
112	
113	## The MXBI archive
114	
115	Boot servers are packed into a single **MXBI archive** (slice 4.2+): `kernel/build.rs`'s
116	`build_server(name, dir, …)` builds each server crate into the shared nested `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`
117	`target/minixrs-user`, `pack_mxbi` concatenates them under a 16-byte header (`magic "MXBI"` / ver /
118	count / total) plus 32-byte records `{proc_nr:i32, offset:u32, len:u32, name:[u8;20]}` (all LE), and
119	emits `BOOT_IMAGE_PATH`.
120	
121	To add a boot server, append a `(crate, dir, proc_nr)` row to the `servers` array (proc_nr from
122	`kernel-shared/com.rs`) and watch its `src` dir. The `env!("BOOT_IMAGE_PATH")` `include_bytes!`
123	lives only in `boot_image/mod.rs`, which is `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]` — that gate is what keeps
124	host `cargo check`/`test` (env unset) compiling, so never reference `BOOT_IMAGE_PATH` from a
125	host-compiled module. `boot_image::BootImage::iter()` drives `userland::load_boot_server(nr, elf,
126	stack_va)` (the generalized `vm_bootstrap`); all servers share one `SERVER_STACK_VA` since each has
127	its own TTBR0.
128	
129	No new boot priv wiring is needed — `init_boot_image` already grants every boot server `SRV_T`
130	`ipc_to` over `[0, n_active)`.
131	
132	**A negative `proc_nr` is the exec-only sentinel.** The `userland.rs` load loop skips any negative
133	`proc_nr`, so a module packed under `com::EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR = -1` is resolvable by name through
134	`BootImage::module_by_name` but **never boot-loaded** — no `[as]` line, no proc slot, no priv slot.
135	That is how `userland/worker` gets into the archive as an exec target only (slice 4.7 — see
136	[phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
137	
138	**Array position is load-bearing.** DS ordering is a chain — `ds < tty < memory < mfs < vfs` — and
139	it is satisfied only by array position in `kernel/build.rs`, so that a server is in its receive loop
140	before its first client looks it up (slice 5.8 — see
141	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
142	
143	## DS: discovering peers
144	
145	Servers discover each other via **DS** (the name→endpoint registry, `servers/ds/`): every server
146	publishes its endpoint at SEF init by setting `init_fresh: Some(...)` to a callback that calls
147	`server-rt::sef_publish_to_ds(endpoint, name)` (a `DS_PUBLISH` SENDREC; key = 16-byte NUL-padded
148	name in payload `0..16`, endpoint `i32` in `16..20`).
149	
150	**DS is the exception** — it seeds its *own* entry in-process in `ds_init` (`registry::publish(name,
151	endpoint)`), because a SENDREC to itself before reaching its receive loop would deadlock. The
152	registry is a static `[Entry; 16]` `UnsafeCell` newtype like `vm/region.rs`; its pure
153	`publish`/`retrieve`/`check` are host-tested, the SEF/IPC `main.rs` is coverage-excluded (add each
154	new server `main.rs`, glob-covered, plus any new `server-rt` IPC-trap module like `ds.rs`
155	explicitly, to `sonar.coverage.exclusions`).
156	
157	**Publish-before-retrieve is not deterministic.** It holds only because of the packing order above,
158	so every DS lookup must **fall back to `boot_endpoint(…)`** and emit a distinguishable diag line —
159	that keeps the rest of the proof alive while only the `*.ds ok` marker for that lookup disappears
160	(slices 5.3 and 5.8 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
161	
162	## Privilege wiring
163	
164	`init_boot_image` fills a boot server's `ipc_to` only for active boot priv slots `[0, n_active)`
165	(~0–15). A hand-installed stub in a higher priv slot (16+) that a server must *reply* to needs the
166	reverse `ipc_to` bit opened explicitly — see `install_stub_d_priv` opening VM→D after setting D→VM.
167	
168	The shared user priv slot is the same shape: `populate_user_priv`'s `USER_IPC_TO` widens
169	`USER_PRIV_ID` (slot 20), and **every entry costs a pair of bits**, because the slot is above
170	`n_active`. Drop the forward bit and a client's SENDREC is refused and every downstream marker
171	vanishes; drop the reverse and the request still *happens* and only the reply is refused, so the
172	client hangs mid-SENDREC and takes the rest of its cycle's markers with it (slice 5.4 — see
173	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
174	
175	## VM: regions and unmapping
176	
177	VM (`servers/vm/`) tracks per-process memory as a static `[ClientRegions; 16]` keyed by proc number
178	(no heap allocator — the kernel owns frames), each region a half-open `[start, end)` tagged
179	`Kind::{Heap, Mmap, Unused}`. A page fault is satisfied only when its address lies inside a region;
180	out-of-region faults are a silent SIGSEGV (faulter left blocked on `RTS_PAGEFAULT` — real signals
181	are Phase 4). `VM_BRK`/`VM_MMAP`/`VM_MUNMAP` all ride the single D→VM SENDREC edge, so adding an
182	mmap client needs no new priv wiring beyond the brk one.
183	
184	`SYS_VMCTL(VMCTL_PT_UNMAP)` returns `EINVAL` (no panic, no frame freed) when nothing is mapped at
185	the target VA — so VM's `munmap` can sweep a region page-by-page with `VMCTL_PT_UNMAP` and ignore
186	the never-faulted pages. Keep the unmap sweep capped at the region's own `end` so an overstated
187	`len` can't reach a neighbour's frames.
188	
189	A region base is not enough on its own: two regions grow on request (the mmap bump cursor, and the
190	heap's end via `set_brk`), so **both** carry a runtime `region::REGION_LIMIT` check (`ENOMEM` past
191	it). `REGION_LIMIT` is the base of the lowest kernel-owned VA window, which is why adding a window
192	above it needs no VM edit — see [kernel.md](./kernel.md).
193	
194	## PM: the process lifecycle
195	
196	**A user process drives its whole lifecycle through PM, never through the kernel.** That is the
197	POSIX shape — user → PM for `PM_FORK`/`PM_EXIT`/`PM_WAIT`/`PM_EXEC`, and PM issues the kernel calls
198	on the caller's behalf. The shared `USER_PRIV_ID` was opened `ipc_to = {PM}` alone for exactly that
199	reason (widened to `{PM, VFS}` in slice 5.4) (slice 4.6b — see
200	[phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
201	
202	### `handle_fork`: a fixed order the frozen-child invariant depends on
203	
204	PM owns the whole tree, in this order and no other:
205	
206	1. allocate an `mproc` child slot from the fork pool `[FORK_POOL_BASE = NR_BOOT_PROCS +
207	   NR_STUB_PROCS, NR_MPROCS = 32)` — **the slot index *is* the child's kernel proc-nr**, so the
208	   pool's base moves with the stub count (see [build-and-boot.md](./build-and-boot.md));
209	2. `SYS_FORK(parent_e, child_nr)`;
210	3. `VM_FORK(parent_e, child_e)`;
211	4. `SCHEDULING_START`;
212	5. `SYS_PRIVCTL(PRIVCTL_SET_USER)` release;
213	6. reply to **both** halves of the shared SENDREC — child `m_type = 0`, parent `m_type = child_pid`
214	   (MINIX fork-returns-twice).
215	
216	**Why the order is safe:** `do_fork` creates the child `RTS_RECEIVING | RTS_NO_PRIV` (frozen), and
217	`sched::rts_unset` enqueues only when the *last* block bit clears — so steps 4 and 5 each leave the
218	child a blocked receiver off the run queue, and **only PM's reply** (clearing `RTS_RECEIVING`) makes
219	it runnable. The child therefore cannot run before its identity, memory and scheduling are built.
220	
221	**PM rolls back at every step.** `SYS_FORK`, `VM_FORK`, `SCHEDULING_START` and `SYS_PRIVCTL` each
222	check their result and, on error, `SYS_EXIT` the child plus `mproc::cleanup` the slot before
223	returning the errno to the parent. The post-`SCHEDULING_START` rollback does `SCHEDULING_STOP`
224	**first**, while the endpoint is still valid — mirroring `handle_exit`. The last two steps are
225	boot-server-backed and cannot fail with correct wiring, so their guards are defence in depth against
226	ever recording an unrunnable child, which would hang the parent's `wait()` forever.
227	
228	Fork needs **no new priv wiring**: PM↔VM and PM↔SCHED are boot-server `[0, n_active)` edges, and
229	child↔PM is the `USER_PRIV_ID` edge.
230	
231	VM's half is `region::fork(parent_nr, child_nr)`, which copies the **whole `ClientRegions`** as a
232	`Copy` snapshot (slice 4.6b — see [phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
233	
234	### `handle_exit` and `handle_wait`
235	
236	- **`SCHEDULING_STOP` before `SYS_EXIT`, always** — once `SYS_EXIT` bumps the endpoint generation,
237	  `okendpt` rejects the endpoint and the stop can no longer be issued.
238	- PM then marks the `mproc` slot a zombie holding the encoded status (`W_EXITCODE = (status & 0xff)
239	  << 8`), and **sends the dead child no reply**.
240	- `handle_wait` either reaps a zombie child (reply pid + status, then `cleanup` the slot) or, with a
241	  live child, sets `MF_WAITING` and **suspends** the parent with no reply until `handle_exit` wakes
242	  it directly.
243	- **There is no async `SIGCHLD`.** The kernel signal path default-*terminates*, which would kill a
244	  handler-less parent, so parent-notify is the zombie plus wait-reap handshake and nothing else
245	  (slice 4.6b — see [phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
246	
247	### `mproc` keeps its logic host-testable
248	
249	`servers/pm/src/mproc.rs` stores a generation-aware `endpoint` per slot (`boot_endpoint(slot)` for
250	seeded procs, the `SYS_FORK` reply for children) plus `exit_status` and `MF_WAITING`. Put the
251	free-slot allocator, the zombie marking and the reap in pure `*_in` helpers that take the slot table
252	as a parameter — that is what makes them host-tested with no IPC (slice 4.6b — see
253	[phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
254	
255	### Draining kernel signals
256	
257	`SYS_GETKSIG` **hands off** the pending-signal bitmap, so PM must dispose of every returned
258	endpoint: `SYS_ENDKSIG` for a survivor, `SYS_EXIT` with **no** `ENDKSIG` after for a termination. A
259	full exit zeroes the signal state and frees the slot, so a post-exit acknowledge just bounces off
260	`okendpt` with `EDEADSRCDST` (slices 4.5 and 4.6a — see
261	[phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
262	
263	## init: PID 1
264	
265	`init` (`INIT_PROC_NR = 10`) is a **real boot process**, not a hand-installed stub: it is packed
266	into the MXBI archive like any server and the ordinary `userland.rs` load loop loads it, clears
267	`RTS_NO_PRIV` and enqueues it — **no PM hand-release**, unlike a frozen stub's `PRIVCTL_SET_USER`.
268	
269	**It carries user-grade privilege, which is the point.** Its `BootEntry.trap_mask` is `USR_T`, not
270	`SRV_T`, and `init_boot_image` special-cases `entry.nr == INIT_PROC_NR` to point its proc slot at
271	the shared `USER_PRIV_ID` instead of populating a dedicated server-grade slot. So init SENDRECs its
272	servers and **makes no kernel calls at all** — exactly the forked-child profile, which is what makes
273	it a usable proof of the user-facing paths.
274	
275	`MF_PRIV_PROC` stays set on init's `mproc` seed (unkillable PID 1). That flag gates only the kill
276	path — not fork, wait or getpid — so PM still serves init as an ordinary client.
277	
278	The `userland/init` crate is **freestanding, like `worker` and not like a server**: dependencies are
279	`minixrs-ipc` and `kernel-shared` only, with **no `server-rt` and no SEF**, its `_start` shim and
280	panic handler are `not(test)`-gated, and its `user.ld` is `worker`'s verbatim (slice 4.8 — see
281	[phase-4-servers.md](../plans/phase-4-servers.md)).
282	
283	## The grant pool: the client side
284	
285	`server-rt::GrantPool<const N>` is **a value the server owns** — a `main`-frame local, never
286	`init_fresh`'s frame. That ownership is what keeps `server-rt` `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`: there is
287	no static to hand out and no interior mutability to justify.
288	
289	`ensure_registered` compares the pool's live address against the last registered one and re-issues
290	`SYS_SETGRANT` if they differ, so a pool that moved is re-registered rather than silently describing
291	the wrong memory. The kernel half of the grant contract is in [kernel.md](./kernel.md); the
292	`GrantEntry` ABI is in [abi.md](./abi.md) (slice 5.2 — see
293	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
294	
295	## Request and reply contracts
296	
297	These bind every band. The band bases and request numbers themselves are in [abi.md](./abi.md).
298	
299	### Always reply
300	
301	A server or driver **replies** to an unknown `m_type` — with `ENOSYS` — where DS may drop one. A
302	driver's and a server's clients all SENDREC, and a dropped request blocks the caller forever (slices
303	5.3 and 5.4 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
304	
305	### Define and refuse, never fold into `ENOSYS`
306	
307	A request you know about but decline gets its own errno, never `ENOSYS` — because `ENOSYS` is
308	already the unknown-`m_type` answer, and reusing it makes "doesn't know about this" and "knows and
309	refuses" indistinguishable. `BDEV_WRITE` was defined this way and answered `EROFS` (it stores for
310	real as of slice 5.10a), and VFS's `do_write` answered `Ok(Fd::File { .. }) => EROFS` rather than
311	folding it into the unused case — in both cases the refusal arm was the one-line landing site for
312	the real implementation (slices 5.7, 5.8 and 5.10a — see
313	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
314	
315	### The granter is `m_source`, never a payload field
316	
317	No request in the CDEV, BDEV or FS bands carries a `granter` field: the server takes it from the
318	kernel-stamped `m_source`. The general confused-deputy rule this follows from is in
319	[abi.md](./abi.md).
320	
321	The rule binds the *granting* side too: when VFS issues a `CPF_MAGIC` grant naming a caller's
322	buffer, the owner is the kernel-stamped `m_source`, never a payload field — VFS holds `SYS_PROC`, so
323	a caller-supplied owner would let any client aim that copy at a third party. **There must never be a
324	field for it.** Same for a control-plane `sys_copy(caller_e, …)`: `SYS_COPY` has no per-target
325	authorization at all, so a payload-supplied source would let any client read any process through the
326	server (slices 5.4, 5.7 and 5.8 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
327	
328	### Short transfers: who may, who may not
329	
330	Reply `m_type` **is the byte count** (`>= 0`) on `CDEV_WRITE`, `CDEV_READ`, `BDEV_READ`,
331	`VFS_WRITE`/`VFS_READ`, `FS_READ` and `FS_WRITE`.
332	
333	- **`CDEV_WRITE` over `CDEV_MAX_IO = 256` is a short write, not a failure** — POSIX `write()`, and
334	  what lets a driver stage through a `main`-frame buffer with no allocator; the client re-sends with
335	  `offset` advanced.
336	- **`CDEV_READ`: `0` is EOF and a short read is legal**, so VFS sends one request and never loops.
337	- **`FS_READ` is clamped — a short read, not `EINVAL`** — and **a short `FS_WRITE` is normal**: the
338	  client is VFS, whose job is hiding staging from POSIX, and a read is short at EOF regardless.
339	- **`BDEV` refuses an over-long or out-of-range request with `EINVAL`, not a short read.** Its
340	  client is a filesystem that cannot interpret half a block. `EIO` stays reserved for Phase 6's real
341	  media errors, where the request was well-formed and the *device* failed.
342	
343	These are not inconsistent: refuse when the client cannot use a fraction, clamp when it can (slices
344	5.3, 5.7, 5.8 and 5.10a — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
345	
346	### Error relay
347	
348	A negative `SYS_SAFECOPY` result is relayed **verbatim** — `EPERM` (bad grant) and `EFAULT`
349	(unmapped buffer) are different client bugs and must stay distinguishable.
350	
351	A `BDEV_READ` failure inside MFS becomes **`EIO`**, because MFS's client addressed a *file*, not a
352	block. The two rules read as contradictory and are not: relay verbatim when the caller owns the
353	object that failed; translate when it does not (slices 5.3 and 5.8 — see
354	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
355	
356	### Control plane travels inline; data travels by grant
357	
358	A path, a name or a key rides **inline in the payload**, NUL-padded to a fixed width — `FS_PATH_OFF`
359	NUL-padded to `FS_PATH_MAX = 64` (so the longest path is 63 bytes, and a field with no NUL is
360	`ENAMETOOLONG` rather than a truncation that could resolve to another file), the `PM_EXEC` name, the
361	`DS_PUBLISH` key. Inline costs the callee no staging buffer — its scarcest resource — and deletes
362	the confused-deputy question, because there is no granter.
363	
364	Data travels by grant with **no granter field and no grant-offset field**. Two shapes follow from
365	that, and both are deliberate:
366	
367	- The CDEV loop advances a payload `offset` against one standing grant.
368	- VFS **re-grants per round** on `FS_WRITE` — a fresh magic grant over exactly the bytes that round
369	  will move, revoked after. Do not add an offset field to buy the other shape: re-granting is what
370	  keeps the confused-deputy surface at zero, and it costs one kernel call a round.
371	
372	`FS_WRITE` reuses `FS_READ`'s payload field for field (inode, grant id, byte count, position) and
373	`FS_CREATE` reuses `FS_LOOKUP`'s wire codec verbatim, request and reply alike — one wire codec and
374	one clamp serve both directions. Only the grant's direction bit differs (`CPF_READ` vs `CPF_WRITE`),
375	checked by the kernel's `verify_grant` and **re-implemented by no server** (slices 5.8, 5.10a and
376	5.10b — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
377	
378	### Don't stub a request nobody consumes
379	
380	A request without a consumer is better absent than stubbed. MFS keeps **no per-open state**, so
381	there is no PUTNODE — which is also why `VFS_CLOSE` sends the FS nothing — and `FS_LOOKUP`'s reply
382	carries mode and size instead of a separate stat (slice 5.8 — see
383	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
384	
385	## The one-page stack
386	
387	A server gets exactly `uspace::SERVER_STACK_BYTES` — one page. Overrunning it faults into VM's
388	SIGSEGV arm, which prints nothing `tests/qemu-boot.forbidden` catches, so the failure is silent.
389	
390	- **A 4 KiB block buffer is a `.bss` static, not a `main`-frame local.** A local would put the frame
391	  base *below* the mapping. `uspace::SERVER_STACK_BYTES` exists solely to carry `fs/mfs`'s `const _`
392	  tripwire for this, and `userland.rs` const-asserts its own stack mapping against it.
393	- This does **not** contradict TTY's "stage in `main`'s frame, not a static". That rule's
394	  load-bearing half is *the buffer outlives every call that names it*, and a static satisfies it
395	  strictly better — the address never changes, so MFS's grant to MEM is issued once at boot and
396	  `ensure_registered` never re-fires.
397	- **Do not grow a server's stack for a demo.** A small granted buffer is a local (32 bytes in VFS's
398	  retired BDEV demo); a 4096-byte local is the silent fault above.
399	
400	Check the largest stack frame in a built server whenever a handler grows a buffer — the
401	`llvm-objdump` recipe is in [build-and-boot.md](./build-and-boot.md) (slices 5.7 and 5.8 — see
402	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
403	
404	## Drivers
405	
406	### Replying, relaying, and register layouts
407	
408	Beyond the shared contracts above, two driver-specific rules:
409	
410	- PL011 register offsets are **duplicated** in `kernel/src/arch/aarch64/uart.rs` and
411	  `drivers/tty/src/pl011.rs` and cannot be shared: the kernel crate is bare-metal-only and pinned by
412	  `forced-target`, so it can never be a user-space dependency, and a register layout is a hardware
413	  fact, not a shared ABI.
414	- `drivers/tty` deliberately does **not** depend on `minixrs-driver-rt` (a 4-line placeholder) —
415	  Phase 6 makes that move, plus the `kernel/build.rs` watch entry (slice 5.3 — see
416	  [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
417	
418	### Block drivers
419	
420	- **A block driver must not depend on the filesystem format.** The `memory` driver's init check is
421	  device-level: `mkfs-mfs` writes a 32-byte **image header** into block 0's unused boot block (bytes
422	  `0..1024`, which MFS never reads) plus a 32-byte **tail label** in a reserved last zone, and the
423	  driver verifies those. Format-level facts are verified by a *client* through a real BDEV round
424	  trip. Phase 6 unwinds this when virtio-blk replaces MEM under an unchanged MFS.
425	- That header ABI lives in **`kernel-shared::rootfs`** — mkfs writes it, MEM and VFS read it, and
426	  none may depend on the others; `image.rs` re-exports it. `kernel-shared::rootfs` also holds the
427	  image's *contents* (`ROOTFS_MOTD`, `ROOTFS_PATTERN_*`, `ROOTFS_HELLO_PATH`,
428	  `rootfs_pattern_byte`), so a read proof is a *check* against the constant rather than a
429	  transcription of it.
430	- **The driver contains no `unsafe` block and never dereferences its mapping**: client transfers are
431	  `sys_safecopy`, and the boot self-check is `sys_copy(SELF, …, SELF, …)`, so a page that failed to
432	  map is an `EFAULT` *return value* rather than an EL0 abort — hence no MMIO sibling module and no
433	  new Sonar exclusion.
434	- Every step of the kernel's pre-map `.expect()`s: a `let _ = map_page_in(..)` would turn a
435	  non-advancing loop into a one-page ramdisk with 255 leaked frames instead of an `AlreadyMapped`
436	  panic. See [kernel.md](./kernel.md) for the pre-map itself (slice 5.7 — see
437	  [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
438	
439	### Minors are a per-driver namespace
440	
441	`/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` are **CDEV minors 3 and 5 of the memory driver** (MINIX 3's
442	`NULL_DEV`/`ZERO_DEV`) while the same driver's ramdisk is **BDEV minor 0**. The request band tells
443	them apart, and nothing asserts `CDEV_MINOR_*` against `BDEV_MINOR_*`.
444	
445	The four-field CDEV parse lives in **`server-rt::cdev`** now that two drivers decode it;
446	**validation stays per driver**.
447	
448	**The memory driver never clamps.** `CDEV_MAX_IO` protects TTY's stack staging buffer and there is
449	no staging here, so a null or zero write answers the whole count with **no copy at all** — an
450	unmapped buffer *succeeds*, which is Linux's behaviour, so **never aim a `bad-buf` probe at
451	`/dev/null`** — and a zero read fills the whole request from a 256-byte static in `CDEV_MAX_IO`
452	steps, reporting partial progress on a mid-way failure (slice 5.11 — see
453	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
454	
455	### Don't answer for a driver
456	
457	A console `read()` is a real `CDEV_READ` to TTY, which answers `ENOSYS` from its unknown-request arm
458	until Phase 6 gives it RX — the same errno VFS used to guess, now the driver's own answer, so Phase
459	6 adds one TTY arm and touches VFS not at all (slice 5.11 — see
460	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
461	
462	## VFS
463	
464	### Absorbing short writes
465	
466	`CDEV_MAX_IO` is a driver staging detail that must not reach `write()`'s return. VFS's write loop:
467	
468	- re-sends with `offset` advanced over the *same* grant until the buffer is out;
469	- clamps `off` with `.min(len)`, so an over-reporting driver cannot walk past the buffer;
470	- breaks on `n == 0` rather than spinning;
471	- on an error **after partial progress, reports the progress** (POSIX: those bytes really went out).
472	
473	**VFS does not loop on read** — POSIX allows a short `read()`; it loops on `write` because it may
474	not. `rw.rs` (formerly `write.rs`) holds the direction-agnostic step logic, since "a peer reporting
475	0" is EOF on a read and a stall on a write, and `advance`'s rules are otherwise identical; `open.rs`
476	holds what differs.
477	
478	**Lift a retry loop's body into a step function.** A retry loop's rules for a misbehaving peer — a
479	driver reporting `0`, or more than it was asked for — are unreachable while the peer works, so a
480	pure step function is the only way to test them. It also keeps them Sonar-measured, since `main.rs`
481	is coverage-excluded and a sibling module is not (slices 5.4 and 5.8 — see
482	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
483	
484	### Grants on the write path
485	
486	VFS is the granter: `do_write` issues a **`CPF_MAGIC` grant naming the caller's buffer with the
487	driver as grantee**, so the bytes move in **one** copy, caller → driver, and VFS never touches them.
488	The owner is `m_source` — see the confused-deputy rule above.
489	
490	`user_range_ok` in `do_write` is **defence in depth, not the gate**: removing it moves no marker,
491	because the kernel's page-table walk answers `EFAULT` regardless (slice 5.4 — see
492	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
493	
494	### The fd table
495	
496	`servers/vfs/src/fd.rs`:
497	
498	- `NR_FDS` is **VFS-local, not ABI**. Both of its sizings were chosen to keep a failure mode
499	  distinguishable: at `4`, the 4th slot made "past the end" and "not open" distinct; raised 4 → 8,
500	  it makes "lowest free" and "table full" distinct tests. Rows are sized from `com::NR_SERVED_PROCS`
501	  with the usual `const _` guard, and fds 0/1/2 are pre-opened to `CDEV_MINOR_CONSOLE` in every row.
502	- `Fd::File { ino, pos }` carries **no cached size** — EOF is `n == 0`, one source of truth, and a
503	  cached size is exactly what a write path would invalidate.
504	- `Fd::CharDev { dev: CharDriver, minor }` names its driver with an **enum, not an `Endpoint`**,
505	  because `DEFAULT_ROW` is a `const`.
506	- Storage is an interior-mutable `UnsafeCell<[FdRow; N]>` newtype (the `vm/region.rs` shape),
507	  **whose rule is never hold a table borrow across a SENDREC**. `Fd` is `Copy`, so the borrow dies
508	  at the destructuring `let`.
509	- **`resolve_in` takes the rows as a borrowed slice, and that is design-for-change, not style.** The
510	  table was an immutable `static` while nothing mutated it (which is how VFS kept zero `unsafe`);
511	  taking a borrowed slice is precisely what let it survive the switch to the `UnsafeCell<[FdRow;
512	  N]>` newtype untouched. Write a pure table helper that way from the start.
513	- **`alloc_in` scans upwards** from fd 3. A `.rposition()` returns 7 and passes every "did I get a
514	  descriptor" check (slices 5.4 and 5.8 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
515	
516	### The device-node table
517	
518	`servers/vfs/src/dev.rs` is a three-row device-node table consulted **after the path copy and before
519	the mount** — a device open needs no filesystem. `O_CREAT`/`O_TRUNC` are ignored on a hit, the match
520	is exact bytes (there is no `/dev` on the image), and `/dev/other` falls through to MFS's `ENOENT`.
521	Paths are `callnr::DEV_*_PATH` so clients and VFS cannot drift (slice 5.11 — see
522	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
523	
524	### Open flags and dispatch
525	
526	`VFS_OPEN` gained `VFS_FLAGS_OFF` (an `i32`, `fcntl`'s values) without moving `NR_VFS_MSGS` — a new
527	*field* on an existing request, not a new request. Dispatch:
528	
529	- `O_CREAT` on a lookup miss → `FS_CREATE`;
530	- `O_TRUNC` on a lookup hit → `FS_TRUNC`;
531	- `O_CREAT | O_TRUNC` on a miss takes the create arm and **stops**, because a fresh file is already
532	  empty.
533	
534	So the truncate, when it runs at all, runs **before the descriptor is installed**, and a failure
535	never leaves a descriptor onto a half-truncated file (slice 5.10b — see
536	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
537	
538	### Prologue ordering
539	
540	VFS's probe batteries run in a fixed order in `main`'s prologue, each new one appended **last** (the
541	retired BDEV demo, then `fs.deny`, then `mem.deny`), so that a hang localizes to the newest battery
542	instead of blacking out every earlier slice's markers. **Do not tidy the prologue into alphabetical
543	order** (slices 5.7 and 5.11 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
544	
545	## MFS
546	
547	### Crate shape
548	
549	`fs/mfs` is split unusually hard because `[[bin]] required-features = ["server"]` removes `main.rs`
550	from every CI job (clippy `--all-targets`, miri, llvm-cov — none passes the feature): **every line
551	with a decision in it is in the lib** (`proto.rs` wire codec, `walk.rs` traversal and read policy,
552	the `Vec`-free rewrite of `mkfs-mfs`'s `verify.rs`). See [ci.md](./ci.md) for the extra `cargo
553	clippy -p minixrs-mfs --features server` step; `kernel/build.rs` threads `--features server` through
554	the nested build the way it threads PM's `--no-default-features`.
555	
556	`proto.rs` re-derives its own `rd_i32`/`rd_u64` because `server-rt` is an *optional* dependency —
557	the trade `userland/init` already makes.
558	
559	The crate is `no_std`, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and has **one dependency** — keep all three: an
560	`unsafe`-free filesystem with a single dep is what lets its decisions be host-tested and
561	geiger-clean while the server half is invisible to CI.
562	
563	The read path (`superblock`/`inode`/`dirent`/`layout`/`read`) is **I/O-free by construction**: every
564	reader takes bytes the caller already fetched. That is both what makes it host-testable with no fake
565	device and the shape the server needs. `zone_for_offset` distinguishes a `Hole` (reads as zeroes)
566	from `OutOfRange` (past the single-indirect span) — explicit, never silent zeroes (slices 5.7 and
567	5.8 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
568	
569	### Degraded, never fatal
570	
571	MFS is **degraded, never fatal and never a panic** past `sef_startup`: a failed mount means `ENODEV`
572	to everything, the `memory` driver's `blocks = 0` precedent.
573	
574	**Every device-derived loop bound has a cap** — `walk::dir_size`'s `MAX_DIR_BYTES`, `size < 0 →
575	EIO`, `zone_ok` before every read. A corrupt `size = i32::MAX` would otherwise spin MFS, blocking
576	VFS, blocking init. VFS's probes cannot reach that class, which is why it needs unit tests (slice
577	5.8 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
578	
579	### Two copies, not one
580	
581	A `FS_READ` is **two copies** — device → MFS's block buffer → the caller's granted buffer — unlike
582	the write path's single caller-to-driver copy. A MinixFS read is rarely block-aligned at both ends,
583	and a *hole* has no device block to copy from at all. This is MINIX 3's own shape (slice 5.8 — see
584	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
585	
586	### Capability tokens: the `Blocks` shape
587	
588	MFS's single block buffer is reached only through the **`Blocks` capability token**, whose
589	`read(&mut self) -> Result<&[u8; N], i32>` makes "hold a directory block across the next fetch" a
590	**borrow-check error** rather than a comment. `Blocks` also carries `buf_mut` and `write`, and its
591	standing grant to the `memory` driver is **`CPF_READ | CPF_WRITE`** — one buffer, both directions,
592	one static address, so `ensure_registered` still never re-fires.
593	
594	Widening those flags does **not** widen what any one call may do (the kernel checks the direction
595	per call), but it *does* re-arm anything that used the pool's grant id as a
596	deliberately-insufficient grant: a denial probe leaning on the narrow flags needs its own narrower
597	grant, aimed at a spare block (`START_BLOCK = 2` leaves block 1 free), in the same change — or the
598	probe writes the block buffer over the superblock (slices 5.8 and 5.10a — see
599	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
600	
601	### What the single block buffer forces
602	
603	MFS has exactly one 4 KiB `.bss` block buffer, and that constraint — not taste — fixes `do_write`'s
604	step order: **read the inode, clamp, compute the grown size, place the zone, read-modify-write the
605	data block, write the inode back.** Nothing may hold a block across the next fetch, so every
606	intermediate is a `Copy` scalar and `place_zone` must finish with the buffer free (slice 5.10a — see
607	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
608	
609	### Allocation ordering
610	
611	- **A zone's bitmap bit is set before its number is stored**, so a mid-write failure leaks a zone
612	  rather than letting two files share one — the recoverable failure over the corrupting one.
613	- **The inode write-back is keyed on "a zone was assigned *or* the size grew", never on the size
614	  alone.** Filling a hole in the middle of an existing file assigns `zone[i]` without moving `size`
615	  at all; keying on size would drop that pointer while leaving its bitmap bit set, so the bitmap and
616	  the inode would disagree about a live zone — corruption rather than a leak.
617	- `do_trunc` frees before writing the inode back, and `create` writes the inode before inserting the
618	  dirent. Neither ordering is provable at the boot-log layer; keep them anyway (slice 5.10b — see
619	  [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
620	- `find_free_slot` must let **`Occupied` beat `Free` across *every* block of a directory, not just
621	  within one**. Scanning block-by-block and returning the first free slot is backwards: a name that
622	  already exists in a later block gets shadowed by a duplicate insert into an earlier block's free
623	  slot — silently, no error, no marker. Scan every block for the name first, and only then reuse a
624	  free slot (slices 5.10a and 5.10b — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
625	
626	### Stage before you allocate
627	
628	`do_write`'s create path copies the client's bytes into a second 4 KiB `.bss` buffer **before
629	anything is allocated**, so no client-controlled failure can occur after an allocation.
630	
631	Do **not** "fix" such a path by clearing the bitmap bit on the error arm: for an indirect slot whose
632	indirect block already existed on disk, the block still names the zone, so freeing the bit hands one
633	zone to two files — corruption rather than a leak (slice 5.10b — see
634	[phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
635	
636	## Writing probes and denial batteries
637	
638	A server's probe battery is how these rules stay proved. Three rules for writing one:
639	
640	- **Write every denial probe so that a growing capability makes it fail loudly, not pass
641	  vacuously.** A probe asserting `EROFS` from `write()` on a file descriptor stopped being a denial
642	  the moment the write path became real, and silently became a successful overwrite — with every
643	  other marker still green.
644	- **Spell an unknown-request probe band-relative** (`VFS_RQ_BASE + NR_VFS_MSGS as i32`), never as a
645	  literal neighbour of an existing request. `VFS_WRITE + 1` became a real `VFS_OPEN` the moment the
646	  band grew. Spell a flag probe relative to the known set the same way: `fcntl::O_UNKNOWN_BIT` is
647	  *derived* from `O_KNOWN`, so a flag becoming real makes the probe fail loudly.
648	- **Never aim a "must be refused" probe at a file or block whose accidental write would destroy
649	  something**, and retire a probe visibly — decrement the `n=` in its marker so the retirement is a
650	  diff rather than a deletion nobody reviews.
651	
652	Report through the path under test where that is what is being proved: a client's write proof must
653	be written **through** the descriptor under test (e.g. `/dev/console`, never fd 1), because the
654	descriptor is the only thing that proves the table row points where it claims (slices 5.8, 5.10a,
655	5.10b and 5.11 — see [phase-5-musl-fs.md](../plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md)).
656
